title: Forces & Motion - Foundations
welcome_lead: Meet the invisible pushes and pulls that shape our universe.
meta_desc: KS3 Physics: learn the basics of forces, types of forces, and how they affect motion.
final_note: You've grasped the basics of forces - the universe's invisible hands!

concepts.def: A push or pull, measured in newtons (N).
Force needing objects to touch, e.g. friction.
Force acting at a distance, e.g. gravity.
Amount of matter in an object, in kilograms.
Force of gravity on a mass, measured in newtons.

walkthroughs.body_html:
A force is simply a push or a pull. You can't see forces, but you can see what they do.

Forces are measured in newtons (N), named after Sir Isaac Newton. A small apple weighs about 1 N.

Forces can make things start moving, stop moving, speed up, slow down, or change direction.

Contact forces only work when things touch. Examples: friction, air resistance, tension in a rope.

Non-contact forces act across a gap. The three main ones are gravity, magnetism, and electrostatic forces.

The Moon pulls Earth's oceans without touching them - that's gravity at work!

People mix these up, but they're different!

Mass = how much stuff is in you. It stays the same everywhere (kg).

Weight = the pull of gravity on your mass. It changes on different planets (N).

On the Moon, your mass is the same, but your weight is about 1/6 of Earth's!

mcqs.q: What unit is force measured in?

numericals.q: A bag has a mass of 5 kg. On Earth, gravity is 10 N/kg. What is its weight in newtons?

free_texts.q: What is the name of the force that opposes motion between two surfaces?
free_texts.hint: It makes rubbing your hands warm.
